This is probably over simplifying it, but it seems like a good regulation would simply be that any self driving car must meet these standards:

  1. It must be programmed with the traffic regulations of all 50 states, and be able to switch these programs based on its gps coordinates.

Austriae est imperare orbi universo

The Reign of King Albrecht IV von Habsburg

Diary of the King:

January 10, 1356

Today the sun rose, and for the first time following my coronation I ruled Austria for an entire day. God willing, my reign will be long and prosperous. I took my first moves as leader of our family empire. The Golden Decree has been declared, and the German princes have agreed to a new type of Empire, a Holy Roman Empire. Together the German princes shall restore the Christian empire of old, and seek to counter the growing threat posed by the Ottomans and their Balkan ambitions.

This morning I met with my royal advisers and took moves to solidify the military. While I am hopeful that we can reach an accord with the Bohemian king to the north, this newfangled Holy Roman Empire creation is sure to create friction in the future. In the meantime, I feel compelled to secure my lands in Italy, which the treacherous Milanese have controlled for far too long. I have ordered the recruitment of over 8,000 men to supplement our existing Royal armies...shortly, the Milanese will learn the meaning of Habsburg vengeance. The royal cabinet has secured the services of some military experts to bolster our forces even further, and to develop future technologies. Some artist stopped by the court asking for money to create some grand tapestry of the Habsburg family history. Despite the exorbitant cost, my family name must grow in prestige if I hope to secure the Emporer election, should Phillipe II suffer some unfortunate demise. Rumor has it that Charles VI de Valois covets the Burgundian lands; I'm not sure whether to root for him, or defend my Germanic brothers, despite their foolish and ill-tempered leader. We shall see what the times bring.

Still, I can't shake the feeling that Bohemia has some terrible ordeal planned for the lands of the Habsburg family. I have reached out to the ruler of Brandenburg, Wilhelm Frederick. I hope to solidify an alliance with him and the House of Hesse-Kassel, which currently rules Palatinae. Together, the three of us may be able to withstand any Bohemian aggression. Tomorrow should bring news of our efforts on that front, as we move to attack the forces of King Colonna and his Milanese peasants.

Finally, I need a wife. I have looked to the Hungarian lands to the east, and I am hopeful to secure their Princess' hand in marriage. As our neighbor, Hungary can provide a much needed counterweight to any potential Bohemian aggression. Honestly, the excitement is starting to wear off, and I think I may need a partner for this journey.

January 11, 1356

Today's first light has brought miraculous news. All of our diplomatic efforts have succeeded, and with lightning speed. The King of Hungary has agreed to marry his daughter, the legendarily beautiful princess, to my family. The King of Bohemia has agreed to a military accord between our families, as has the ruler of the Palatinae lands.

As if this weren't a political coup of it's own accord, this afternoon riders returned from Brandeburg bearing more goods news. They have also agreed to our military alliance request. For now, before I declare war upon Milan, this looks to be a perfect situation. I am concerned that should Bohemia and Brandenburg come to blows, however, that we may become caught in the middle. It is already a complicated web this new Empire is weaving.

Speaking of which, sending a gift to the new Emporer, His most Holy Roman Emporer Phillipe the 2nd, is now a priority. Until he dies, there will be no new elections, and I am stuck playing second fiddle to that half Gaul bastard child. I will bide my time however, and seek strong alliances in the meantime. Speaking of which, the Danes sent an envoy today and requested an alliance. I think I will defer making a decision until the end of the month, and see what the war against Milan brings. It is best not to over commit ourselves, at this time.

Tomorrow I assume command of the K.u.K. and ride towards the Milanese border. Brescia, Verona and Cremona have been in their grasp for far too long. I pray for good fortune. A.E.I.O.U.

January 11, 1356

January 12, 1356

This morning, we ride. While my second army is in training, I will ride out with my Royal army to meet the Milanese on the borderlands.

I was initially concerned that such early action could endanger our new alliances, but Brandenburg, Bohemia and the Palatinae have all agreed to support my invasion. I also had a change of heart and quickly accepted the Danes offer of an alliance and invoked the treaty to bring them against the Milanese, as well. Things are looking bleak for the Milanese.

It may be some time before I write again, but I hope to bring news of glory for the Habsburgs.

February 12, 1356

The past month has been a long ride across the Austrian lands, and we have almost reached the Tirol province. The forces of Milan are moving on Trent, and since our journey has taken longer than anticipated, we may find ourselves on poor footing entering the province. Surprisingly, the King of Sicily has agreed to join in the defense of Milan, but given his limited resources to secure even his own country, I do not fear him very much.

Aside from those issues, The Royal advisers have informed me that numerous delegates have arrived from some of the more minor German states. We have agreed to marry off enough Habsburg cousins to ingratiate ourselves by blood into many of the Royal houses of Europe already. The respect given to the Habsburg name has grown, and in only a month. Soon, I will taste the victory of combat, Lord willing.

February 20th, 1356

TREACHERY! The diseased Aquileans have declared war on Austria, also coming to Milan's defense. While this may work to our advantage in the long run, I must admit I did not foresee this coming. Hopefully the Bohemian King will make good on his promises and hold the Aquileans at bay, so I can focus on the Milanese. Of course, I have no guarantees that the Bohemians will leave one they enter Austria, so my I am feeling quite vulnerable at the moment. This step may have been a bit too audacious, even for a Habsburg.

Upon further reflection, I have decided to turn south and punish the Aquileans. The Milanese are still tied up pacifying Trent, and I may have the opportunity to occupy Aquilea before turning towards the real prize. Scouts have brought word that Bohemian troops are on the move south towards Austria. Perhaps, I will let the Bohemians confront the Milanese and see if we can't position our armies to occupy the cities before the Bohemians.

May 12, 1356**

Victory was not quite as swift as I had hoped, but it was complete. The armies of Aquilea have been totally destroyed. 2,000 Habsburg troops occupy each of their provinces and I have turned the K.u.K towards the province of Trent. The Milanese have been in control since February, and I am growing concerned that the occupation will affect the planting season. Facing a famine come the fall is not a situation I'd like to deal with, especially with an army to feed.

On a brighter note, the Bohemians finally arrived to relieve Trent, and have engaged the Milanese. I have no reports from the battle upon which to rely, but I have decided to ride to Verona. The Venetian Republic has agreed to allow my armies to pass through their territory, though I am sure the price to be paid will come later. Should the Milanese lose, they will likely retreat to Verona and I can cut off their retreat, if I can get the K.u.K. there first. Should the Bohemians simply hold the Milanese to a draw, I can ride north and join the battle in Trent. God willing, this next phase will proceed as smoothly as the first.

Our armies have performed wonderfully and suffered minimal casualties. Tomorrow, however, begins the real test.

I have commissioned more engravings and paintings of the past few week's events. They have arrived at camp, and I look forward to viewing them before showing them to the troops. Hopefully, this keeps morale high, while food supplies are starting to dwindle.

The King's Gallery

I have just been awoken by news that Sundgau has fallen to Lorraine and is now under their occupation. My scouts have failed me, for the last time. Many Alsatians died to bring me these battle plans. Lorraine shall pay for this. I swear on my family's honor, I will have their loyalty, by force of arms, or by massacring the entire population in Lorraine and expanding our holdings to the west. My only worry is having lands so close to both Burgundy and France. Perhaps Switzerland is in need of a friend?

On to Milan.

June 20, 1356

The Bohemian and Brandenburger combined armies have lost to Milan in the Trent province. Who would've have thought that a bunch of provincials could take on the might army of Bohemia and win? This is a disaster of epic proportions. My allies have retreated to Tyrol, and the Milanese have turned south. I have the province of Verona under siege, but my troops are preparing defensive positions as the Milanese prepare their attack. I dispatched messengers this morning calling for 7,000 troops to reinforce Verona, but they may not arrive before the Milanese do. Currently, my 8,000 troops are preparing for battle against 14,000 experienced, but tired troops from Milan and it's countryside. Let's hope my forces fare considerably better than the Bohemians did. Should we survive this battle, our alliance with the Bohemians may need to be re-examined; I never imagined them to be such cowards. Perhaps they need some Austrian guidance in the future?

For some morbid reason, an artist decided to commemorate this occasion. I had him drawn and quartered for being so foolish, but the picture isn't too bad. It may turn out to memorialize my greatest victory in the face of overwhelming odds.

AEIOU.

The King's Gallery

September 2, 1356

After an intial setback in Verona, we retreated to Trent, and spent the month repairing our morale. Our reinforcements camped in the Venetian lands, and were well fed by the Republic. Without a doubt, Venice will be sending a healthy bill. After bivouacking for a bit, we marched on Verona and met the Milanese peasants in battle once again. With some assistance from the Bohemians, who seemed to have regained their stomach for battle, we managed to win the day. The Milanese army is still a viable force, but they have retreated towards the waiting Bohemian armies in Brescia. In the meantime, our secondary forces have begun to siege Cremona, and have sent scouts to probe Milan's defense in their capital province.

Things are looking up, but I am hesitant to be overly optimistic. Given the way Bohemia fell apart before, should they do so again, my grip on our Northern Italian provinces will be very tenuous, at best. God willing, things will continue to go well.

My foreign relations adviser arrived today, and the continent seems quiet for the most part, aside from our attempts to claim what is rightfully ours. This eerie calm does not bode well for the future peace. France is plotting something; I wonder against whom?

September 5, 2016

Despite the trouble of writing from the front, today brings news of a unique sort. Hungary has been embroiled in a war against the peasantry and their latest uprising. According to my wife's latest missives, her father is suffering greatly, and may be on the verge of losing control. She has asked me to consider helping her father put down the insurrection.

At this point, his troubles are his own and I am locked in a war in Northern Italy; I fear there is little I can do. As husband of the King of Hungary's daughter, and I myself of noble blood by birth- should the King in Hungary's capability to rule fall any further, I may have to consider making a claim on his throne to protect my heirs. Speaking of which, my wife still has not bore me a son, or even a daughter. Considering how long I've been away for, this is a positive thing, but one that must be addressed sooner rather than later. I must have a male heir to compete for Emperor election.

October 2, 1365

All Glory to God. A child is born to the Habsburg King. On this 2nd of October, the Crown Prince Karl von Habsburg was born. All of Austria rejoices, as her future King is born.

Chants of "ALL HAIL KING ALBRECHT IV" are ringing through the streets, even in our ancestral lands in Northern Italy.

And, our campaign in Italy is a complete success. We have sieged all of Milan's provinces, and still occupy all of Aquilea. Once we control the land completely, I must exact my revenge against Lorraine. That tiny, insignificant principality shall pay for their transgressions.

It has been a long 8 months since I last saw the beautiful Queen, and I am happy to learn of her pregnancy, and of my son all at once. God has truly blessed the Habsburgs.

I have commissioned a map of the kingdom on the day of my son's birth. I want him to see the limits of his kingdom when he was born, for I intend to have it quite a bit larger by the time he takes the throne.

The King's Gallery

AEIOU.

August 19, 1358

Lorraine has been occupied by the Palatinae. Before they could be annexed, former King Rene de Chin I fled in the middle of the night. What an embarrassing escapade for a man of noble birth. Chased from his castle in the middle of the night, he was soon discovered and captured by my scouts.

I met with him this morning, and found him to be an amenable man, despite his cowardly nature. A shrewd politician, if nothing else, he quickly offered to become my vassal. Rather than allow the Palatinae to expand further, I think our interests are better served by maintaining a puppet on the French and Burgundian border. Besides, this gives us some additional defense for Sundgau.

Milan and Aquilea have been under continual occupation for nearly 2 years. Our armies grow restless, and many desire to return home, so I have begun to order the troops back.

Bohemia and Brandenburg are in control of Cremona and Brescia. Austrian forces control the rest of Milan, including the capital. Despite winning this war, it appears I may not get the spoils I had intended. No matter, our prestige within Europe has been considerably raised.

Another victory, another piece of art.

The King's Gallery

February 25, 1362

The last of Aquilean province has fallen. Our enemies our completely annihilated. In the morning I ride out to meet both leaders. I expect to vassalize Aquilea and to cripple Milan. Austria is on the rise. I just hope my actions don't worry the other princes to the point where they start to connive against me.

We shall see what the morning brings.

February 26, 1362

Aquilea has agree to be our vassal. We now have allies to the west and south. Our strength grows by the minute. I expect to reach an agreement with Milan by the morning. Details forthcoming.

February 27, 1362

At long last, my war of conquest has ended. The conflict dragged on longer than I could have imagined. I suppose after the Bohemians initial defeat, I should feel fortunate to have escaped at all, let alone win the war.

We have gained two vassals and nearly doubled our lands in Northern Italy. In addition to my ancestral lands, I have seized Parma. What that imbecile, the Holy Roman Burgundian Fool, tries to do about it remains to be seen. I do expect some kind of repercussions, but after our victories, I think anyone....,even the Emperor, would be hesitant to confront us while at the height of our power. Internally, we are stable and our manpower reserves are surprisingly robust considering the long conflict we were just in. Our treasury is full and our armies are riding the wave of victory.

All the same, these soldiers have families, and it's about time I returned to mine. Looking forward to springtime in Vienna.

Hopefully pacifying these lands will not prove as difficult as obtaining them has been.

In the meantime, the celebration awaits.

AEIOU
